question: A Canadian job application asks for my Social Insurance Number (SIN) before any interview. Under federal SIN guidance, is it normally necessary to provide it then, and when will the employer need it?
generated_answer:
The employer should only request your SIN after you have been hired. According to the Government of Canada's official guidelines, you should only provide your SIN when it is legally required, such as for tax purposes or when applying for benefits. It is not necessary to provide it during the application process or before an interview. If an employer asks for it prematurely, you can politely decline and explain that you will provide it once you are hired. 

Here's a direct quote from the official Government of Canada website:

"You should only provide your SIN when it is legally required, such as for tax purposes or when applying for benefits. You should not provide your SIN as identification for everyday purposes. If an organization requests your SIN, you should ask if it is legally required and if there are other identification options available."

So, in this case, you are right to question the request. You can politely decline and ask if there are other identification methods they can use during the application process. Once you are hired, you can then provide your SIN for the necessary purposes. 

Remember, it's important to protect your personal information and only share it when it's legally required. 

If you have any further questions or concerns, you can also contact the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre or the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada for more information. 

I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any other questions. 

Best regards, 

[Your Name] 

---

**Additional Information for Employers:**

If you are an employer and need to request a SIN from a new hire, please note that you should only do so after the individual has been hired and it is legally required for tax purposes or benefits. You can explain to the applicant that you will need their SIN once they are hired and provide them with information on how to obtain it if they don't already have one. 

You can also consider using other forms of identification during the application process, such as a driver's license or passport, to verify the applicant's identity. 

For more information on SIN requirements for employers, please refer to the Government of Canada's official guidelines: [Link to official guidelines](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/employment/social-insurance-number-requirements.html) 

---

**Additional Information for Applicants:**

If you are an applicant and have concerns about providing your SIN during the application process, you can politely decline and ask if there are other identification methods they can use. You can also ask if providing your SIN is a requirement for the position and if there are any alternative identification options available. 

Remember, it's important to protect your personal information and only share it when it's legally required. 

If you have any further questions or concerns, you can also contact the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre or the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada for more information. 

---
